newsitem.title: USA: Conrail reaches property tax settlement.
newsitem.headline: Conrail reaches property tax settlement.

text.p: Conrail Inc said Monday it expects to pay an estimated $27.5 million annually in property taxes over an eight-year period as part of a settlement with New York State.
The settlement was filed February 7 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.
The settlement amount is subject to changing tax rates and adjustments for property transactions, Conrail said.
U.S. Justice Charles L. Brieant is to rule on the proposed settlement at a hearing scheduled for April 16.

The property tax dispute began in 1993, when Conrail filed a class action suit in federal court against all of the New York state taxing jurisdictions in which it operates, as well as the New York State Board of Equalization and Assessment, which is now called the Office of Real Property Services.

The railroad claimed its property was assessed and taxed at higher levels than other commercial and industrial property in violation of the federal Railroad Revitalization and Regulatory Reform Act of 1976.
The settlement is retroactive to 1993 and carries forward to 2000, when "we'll be back where we are now," Conrail spokesman Rudy Husband said.

Since the filing of the suit in 1993, Conrail has continued to pay both undisputed and disputed taxes to school districts, but has placed the disputed portion of municipal taxes into an escrow account.
